QUESTION OF THE WEEK - After Wednesday's decision by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to cut interest rates to 6.0 percent, a move that caught many off guard, economists were asked their view on the likelihood of another interest rate cut.

The chances are put at slightly less than 50 percent, and if it has not happened by the end of the first quarter of next year, then the chances of a cut will diminish, economists said. February and March are seen as the most likely months, following the release of December quarter inflation and wages data.

While the likelihood of a cut has decreased and the prospects for the economy in 1997 had improved, some economists said chances of another cut remained reasonably high as the inflation outlook was expected to improve and the RBA had signalled it would seek higher growth to reduce unemployment.

Some economists felt the cut would happen in March because by then the RBA would have received another three months of employmemt data and would be able to see whether employment strength seen in the last two months has carried through.

One reason why a cut may not occur until the June quarter would be that the RBA may wait and see the extent of fiscal tightening in the May budget, and its likely impact on growth and employment. ----------------------------------------------------------------

MERCHANDISE IMPORTS - Wednesday's release is generally seen as the last piece of potentially market moving data in 1996. Imports are expected to show their fourth consecutive monthly rise, aided by the inclusion of an aircraft which could be worth up to around A$120 million, economists said. A rise in line with median forecasts would take them to their highest level since May, which was also the month in which the highest current account deficit for the year was recorded.
